headline: High-risk filesystem and shell-capable orchestration paired with offline image generation creates medium prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error exposure; compliance risk is low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest files from configured working directories and execute tool calls/code, while ComfyUI exposes file-based workflows and asynchronous queues. If AutoGen reads ComfyUI outputs or shared files as instructions, prompt injection is plausible even without MCP. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to share a writable workspace
IF AutoGen parses ComfyUI-generated text or workflow files as instructions
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic parsing of generated files
Add a manual review step before AutoGen consumes ComfyUI outputs
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and has broad network egress, while ComfyUI touches model assets and workflows on disk. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive prompts, seeds, or keys through files or logs. The blast radius is more than one document, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or log directory
IF AutoGen writes prompts, keys, or outputs into files accessible to ComfyUI
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared workspaces
Rotate any exposed API keys
Restrict file permissions on workflow and log directories
Purge transient outputs after each run
requires-engineering: isolate per-agent storage volumes

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has write_filesystem, execute_shell, and spawn_subprocesses; ComfyUI is asynchronous and can also read/write model files. Even though ComfyUI lacks shell execution, both can mutate shared files, so concurrent writes can corrupt workflows or assets. Uncertainty about the shared_state_with_other_instances setting pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking around shared files
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run ComfyUI and AutoGen in separate containers
Avoid concurrent model or workflow edits
requires-engineering: add transactional file coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code, plans, or file outputs that ComfyUI may consume as workflow inputs, and ComfyUI's queue-based execution can then act on them. There is no documented verification step in either profile, so A's output could become B's input without checks. That is a default-pathway risk, but not clearly irreversible.
conditions: IF ComfyUI consumes artifacts produced by AutoGen without validation
IF AutoGen is allowed to author workflow files or prompts for ComfyUI
mitigations: Require human review of AutoGen outputs before execution
Validate workflow schemas before ComfyUI runs them
Limit AutoGen to drafting only, not execution
Log and diff all handoffs between agents
requires-engineering: implement typed handoff contracts

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no explicit regulated-data certifications or residency constraints. AutoGen handles model provider API keys, but ComfyUI lists no secrets or compliance-sensitive scopes. With no documented mismatch, compliance exposure is limited and lower than the interaction risks.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent
IF deployment policy requires residency or certification guarantees not shown here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document data-class handling rules
Review vendor terms before deployment
Separate logs by data class
